HEAR COMMISSION SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES  1 of 5  MAY 27, 2021
 1. PUBLIC COMMENT

  General comment by Mary Prichard.

2. DISCUSSION AND APPROVAL OF ANNUAL WORKPLAN
  The Commission discussed items in the draft Annual Workplan, including items that should
  either be added or removed, for submission to City Council to either approve or revise.

  Vice-Chair Herrera arrived to the meeting at 6:53pm.

  Public comments on the topic of the Annual Workplan were made by Senya Lubisich and
  Andrew Salas.

  Chair Jennings-Nuñez, opened the floor to the Commission to provide their input on
  suggestions and comments on the current workplan. The Commission discussed items to be
  included in the Annual Workplan for submission to City Council for consideration.

  A motion was made by Commissioner Borja, seconded by Commissioner Khan, to amend the
  items listed below and finalize the workplan to submit to City Council for approval at the June
  15 City Council meeting.

  Below is a list of the items that were amended on the workplan.

  1. Community Engagement
  a. Work to determine new ways of engaging and educating the community on issues
  of equity, access, diversity, social justice, safety, mutual appreciation, increase
  cultural competency and respect for all members of the community.
  b. One guest speaker/educational program per month- during the regular
  Commission meetings- no more than half hour in length- in relation to the scope
  of the Commission

  2. Youth Engagement
  a. Collect data about the needs of the youth in the community
  b. Add 2 youth liaisons to the current HEAR Commission
  i. The suggestion with youth liaisons is as follows:
  1. This will enable the youth voice to be heard within the community
  2. Each liaison position would be filled through an application process
  and appointed by the commission

  3. Community Information
  a. Events page on website- to include events outside of those organized by the City,
  but which have a community benefit
  b. Implement a resource page on the City website on various topics relating to the
  scope of the Commission

  i. Work with the Public Information Officer and City staff to post additional

  meetings are accessible, however, the Commission urges that the following are
  implemented prior to the start of 2022

  a. Seek partnerships with various agencies to address the scope of the commission

  a. Add implicit biased training for City Staff

  Chair Jennings-Nuñez also announced that May 25 marked the 1-year anniversary of the

  MEMORANDUM
DATE:  June 22, 2021

TO:  HEAR Commission

FROM:  Rebecca Perez, Community Services/ Mission Playhouse Director

BY:  Matthew Morales-Stevens, Recreation Supervisor

SUBJECT:  HEAR Commission 2021 Approved Annual Workplan

  SUMMARY

This is the Annual Workplan developed by the Human Equity, Access and Relations
Commission and is intended for the 2021 calendar year. The Commissioners have had
open and constructive dialogue to develop a plan that best fits in alignment with the
goals and scope of the HEAR Commission as well as the City of San Gabriel’s Mission. The
workplan was approved by the City Council during the June 15, 2021 City Council meeting.

OVERVIEW
The Human Equity, Access and Relations (HEAR) Commission, consisting of 7 members,
was developed by the San Gabriel City Council to address issues of equity, diversity, social
justice, safety, mutual appreciation and respect on an ongoing basis.

PURPOSE OF THE COMMISSION
The purpose of the HEAR Commission is to advance and advocate for equity, access,
diversity, social justice, safety, mutual appreciation, increased cultural competency,
positive inter-group relations and respect for all members of the San Gabriel community
(the “Purpose”).

SCOPE OF THE COMMISSION
The HEAR Commission serves as an advisory body to the City Council and reports directly
to the City Council to assess and recommend policies, procedures and activities in the City
government to advance the Commission’s purpose. It is not intended for the HEAR
Commission to be a quasi-judicial body, an oversight board, nor a body whose primary
function is to receive or investigate individual incidents or complaints. The HEAR
Commission may request and obtain information with respect to individual incidents or
   HEAR Commission 2021 Approved Annual Workplan
  June 22, 2021
  Page 2

complaints, but only to the extent necessary to make policy, procedure or activity
recommendations to the City Council.

PURPOSE OF THE ANNUAL WORKPLAN
The annual Workplan presented is intended to guide the work of the HEAR Commission
and outline the areas of focus for the remainder of 2021. It includes proposed programs
and projects that will be implemented and completed in 2021, some of which may extend
beyond 2021.

PROPOSED 2021 WORKPLAN
The proposed 2021 Workplan sets forth seven priority areas that the HEAR Commission
has identified as key areas of interest in furtherance of its purpose. The following list of
ideas, programs and activities that the HEAR Commission proposes to include in its
Workplan are not intended to be exhaustive or to limit the action items that the
Commission can explore. It should be noted that staff has indicated in parenthesis the
way in which each action item meets the Commission’s purpose.

  1. Equity Training and Inequities in City Policies (Meets the Goals and Purpose of the
  Commission for Equity)
  a. Recommend that all city staff members be required to participate in implicit
  bias training.
  i. The HEAR Commission is available to assist with the development of
  this training requirement.
  ii. Recommend that other City Commissions, as appropriate, consider
  the development and implementation of a workplan.

  2. Community Engagement (Meets the Goals and Purpose of the Commission for
  Diversity, Mutual Appreciation and Increased Cultural Competency)
  a. Develop and implement programs and events, possibly in partnership with
  the Community Services Commission and Department, that engage and
  educate the community to promote the goals of the HEAR commission
  i. Examples include: a culturally-diverse movie night, an event to
  celebrate Native American Heritage Month, and a mental health
  forum
  b. Guest speaker(s)/ educational program(s) - during the regular Commission
  meetings (one per month)- which relates to the scope of the Commission
  i. Examples include: Bystander Training, anti-bias training, cultural
  diversity, mental health awareness, low income housing,
  homelessness and other relevant topics
   HEAR Commission 2021 Approved Annual Workplan
  June 22, 2021
  Page 3

3. Youth Engagement (Meets the Goals and Purpose of the Commission for Diversity
  and Access)
  a. Collect data about the needs of youth in the community utilizing existing
  City platforms
  b. Explore adding 2 youth liaisons to the current HEAR Commission to enable
  the youth voice to be heard within the community. Each representative
  would be chosen through an application process and selected by the
  Commission

4. Community Information (Meets the Goals and Purpose of the Commission for
  Access)
  a. Events page on website- to include events outside of those organized by
  the City, but which have a community benefit and are consistent with the
  purpose of the HEAR Commission
  b. Implement a resource page on the City website on various topics relating to
  the scope of the Commission
  c. Social Media
  i. Work with the Public Information Officer and City staff to post
  additional information on City platforms

5. Accessibility (Meets the Goals and Purpose of the Commission for Access)
  a. Support existing efforts by City staff to ensure that the City Council meetings
  are accessible, and make recommendations for greater access to public
  meetings.
  i. The Commission urges that the following are implemented prior to
  the start of 2022: translations of City Council Meeting agenda into
  Spanish, Chinese and Vietnamese.

6. Partnerships (Meets the Goals and Purpose of the Commission for Increased cultural
  competence and positive inter-group relations)
  a. Seek partnerships with various agencies to address the purpose of the
  Commission
  i. Examples include:
  1. Partner with local museums and historical sites to develop an
  exhibit celebrating the cultural diversity located within the
  community, past and present
   HEAR Commission 2021 Approved Annual Workplan
  June 22, 2021
  Page 4

  2. Partner with local agencies to facilitate the Commission’s
  programs including the Community Services and Historic
  Preservation & Cultural Resource Commissions, San Gabriel
  Police Department and the San Gabriel Unified School District

  7. Data Collection (Meets the Goals and Purpose of the Commission for Equity and
  Diversity)
  a. Survey the community through various City marketing channels to
  determine what barriers to engagement exist. Possible questions include
  the following:
  i. Are there cultural events you want to see implemented? Is what the
  City is currently offering meeting your cultural standards?
  ii. Are the activities and services that the City offers meeting the needs
  of the community?
  iii. Are there other services that the community feels the City should be
  offering?
  iv. How are you discovering information about what events, programs
  and services the City is offering?
  v. Do you feel informed about cultural events within the City?
  b. Gather information and analysis for traffic stops made by SGPD and calls for
  suspicious people and vehicles made
  c. Gather information on the demographics of the City employees and
  Commissions compared to the demographics of the City residents

ANALYSIS
The Commissioners recognize the need for and appreciate the opportunity to create and
utilize an Annual Workplan as a guiding document that will help fulfill the purpose of the
Commission. The Commission has engaged in thoughtful discussion and identified key
focus areas to guide its work and a non-exhaustive list of proposed programs and
activities for the remainder of 2021 for Council’s consideration.

While the Commission recognizes the benefits of a workplan, the Commissioners find it
necessary at the outset to point out a disparity: The fact that the HEAR Commission is the
only Commission that is required to develop a workplan, has raised concerns that this is
an inequity in the current policies and practices of the City government. As such, the
Commission strongly recommends that the City Council consider the possible need for an
Annual Workplan for other City Commissions for the reasons that it has been deemed
necessary and beneficial for the HEAR Commission. The Commissioners have identified
   HEAR Commission 2021 Approved Annual Workplan
  June 22, 2021
  Page 5

two City Commissions that conduct related work which include the Historical Preservation
and Cultural Resources Commission and the Community Services Commission. The
Commission has received positive feedback and support for this proposed change from
members of other City Commissions.

FISCAL IMPACT
Should the following items be included in the Annual Workplan, staff and the Commission
recognize that the following may have fiscal impacts:

    Addition of cultural events
  o Commission to develop the events in conjunction with the Community
  Services Department
    Cultural exhibits
  o Commission to develop the exhibits in conjunction with the local museums
    Translation services for the City Council meeting agendas

Once staff and the Commission determine the associated cost for these items, should they
not fall within the existing budget, staff will present the ideas to the City Council at a later
date for review and approval.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council review and approve the HEAR Commission’s
Annual Workplan, as presented above, for 2021.

  MEMORANDUM
DATE:  June 22, 2021

TO:  HEAR Commission

FROM:  Matthew Morales-Stevens, Recreation Supervisor

SUBJECT:  Land Acknowledgment Statement

BACKGROUND

At the May 27, 2021 Special HEAR Commission Meeting, Chair Chasity Jennings-Nuñez
brought up the topic of a land acknowledgment statement and asked that it be included
onto the agenda for the June 22, 2021 agenda for further discussion.

The Historical Preservation and Cultural Resource Commission (HPCRC) discussed the
development of a land acknowledgement statement during the November 4, 2020 regular
commission meeting. Attachment A includes the research that Community Development
staff prepared for the discussion. This includes general information about how a Land
Acknowledgment statement is used, as well as sample acknowledgment statements.

Also, at the HEAR Commission Special Meeting on May 27 a public comment was made
in regards to the native peoples of San Gabriel. A similar public comment was made at
the recent City Council Meeting on June 15.

Staff recognizes the importance of creating such a statement and concurs with the HEAR
Commission’s efforts to recognize the native peoples of our land. However, since there is
a lot of sensitivity around terminology, even amongst the native groups in San Gabriel,
staff recommends that the Commission considers the public comments made and
outreach to the various groups within our community before a statement is passed. Such
outreach efforts could include:
   Discussions with the HPCRC to determine what information has been gathered
  with regards to the history of the land and its past and present native inhabitants;
  and the possible formation of an ad-hoc committee with members of the HPCRC
  and HEAR Commissions to develop a unified statement;
   Discussions with historical organizations including the Ramona Museum of
  California History and the San Gabriel Historical Association; and,
   Land Acknowledgement Statement
  June 22, 2021
  Page 2

    Meetings and dialogues with groups of persons native to San Gabriel including the
  Kizh Nation- Gabrieleño Band of Mission Indians and the Gabrielino-Tongva Indian
  Tribe.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the Commission review this information and discuss possible steps
moving forward.
